name: Parsons Hall
use: Chemistry teaching and research labs, chemistry library, University Instrumentation Center, Iddles Auditorium
builtText: 1965–68 (E/W wings 1965; lecture and classroom wings incl. Iddles Auditorium by 1968); archives index says 1966
architect: Alonzo J. Harriman Associates; builder Harvey Construction
style: 1960s modern: long low brick wings with a columned concrete entrance portico

renovations.what: 1970s solar heating added (no longer used; panels remain)
Major renovation of ~120,000 of 146,224 gsf (EYP design, Gilbane CM), under way from May 2009: new teaching/research labs, Instrumentation Center, sprinklers
1,800 sq ft Advanced Technology Imaging Facility; transmission electron microscope moved in from Kendall Hall (JM Coull, Port City Architecture)
Iddles Wing (13,000 sq ft): two lecture halls, two classrooms, corridors, new HVAC, student commons, new storefront entrance (Chapman; Harriman A/E)

facts.text: Designed by Alonzo J. Harriman Associates and built by Harvey Construction for chemistry; construction began 1965 and finished 1968 with the lecture wings and Iddles Auditorium.
Solar heating added in the 1970s is no longer used, but the panels remain on the roof.
EYP was selected to redesign 120,000 sq ft of the 146,224 gsf building with Gilbane as construction manager.
The Iddles Wing had not been substantially renovated in 50 years before its 2020 project.

verdict: Long, low 1960s brick chemistry wings with a concrete portico, largely renovated from 2009 into modern labs.
notes: Photo (2013) shows a low, long brick-and-precast wing with ribbon windows and rooftop solar tanks, behind a concrete-columned glass entrance; plain 1960s institutional. Completion of the 2009 renovation (~2011) and the ATIF date (2014) come from the old row; opened pages give no completion dates. The 2020 Iddles work is inferred from the Mar 2020 award article (summer schedule); completion not confirmed. Only one licensed photo.
